raw_response:
I farm this land the way I always have to: steady, not fancy. We are 4 people in the house, but some go out to work, so I cannot count on too many hands at the busy time. I have 36 mu, and I will not press all of it into one crop. If one crop goes bad, the whole year goes bad, so I keep maize, cotton, and a little mungbean.

For maize, I will keep the biggest area because it is safer and easier to sell. Cotton can make money, but it eats labor, especially picking, so I will not make it too large. Mungbean I put on a smaller piece because it needs less fertilizer and gives me a cheaper crop to carry. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I will water when the crop really needs it, not just because the well is there. Fertilizer also costs cash. I would rather put a moderate amount and not let the crop go hungry, but I will not chase very high rates because I still need cash in hand for pesticide and household use.
